newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities end lower on weaker Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: German equities end lower on weaker Wall Street.

text.p: Worries about Europe's single currency plans and weak signals from the U.S. and Japan dragged German shares off all-time highs on Friday, but dealers said the market was still poised for further gains next week.

Despite Friday's 0.5 percent drop to 3,259.64 points, the 30-share DAX index, which measures floor trade in German blue-chip stocks, has still risen more than two percent this week. Its record close on Thursday of 3,276.72 points represented a 13 percent rise this year.
And many dealers say more is to come, given that analysts are still in the process of upgrading earnings estimates for German firms in the light of the dollar's dramatic rally.
The IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day electronic trade, ended down 11.54 points or 0.35 percent, at 3,261.04 points.
"What we've seen today was no real pressure. Investors were hardly there at all," said a senior trader at a Bavarian bank.
A Frankfurt dealer said: "I can see more money coming into the market next week. Things should be at least stable with a positive leaning."
Dealers also conceded that market rumours of a statement on a delayed launch of the euro were unrealistic.

Talk of such a statement, to which no market players could ascribe a clear source, had sent prices lower in early bourse trading, as dealers feared that an EMU delay could hurt earnings prospects for exporters.
The decline halted after the Bundesbank and the Finance Ministry denied any such plans, but the thinly-traded market lacked impetus for another advance, dealers said.
Performance was uneven, with a few clear exceptions. Retailer Metro AG ended up 4.65 percent at 148.50 marks, after dealers said the stock had broken above a key technical barrier.

Volkswagen rose to a high of 824 marks in IBIS trade after the carmaker said on Thursday that sales in January rose 18 percent and it expected to maintain its world market share in 1997 despite difficult industry conditions.
The share came off over the day to end at 813 marks, up 50 pfennigs.
